threads.thread_goal: Align on current pain points and approve target tax workflow scope.

messages.text:
Kickoff for the standardised tax documentation and filing workflow. The goal is to have a clear, audit-ready process in place before the next quarterly deadline for project_title: Standardised Tax Documentation & Filing Workflow Rollout.
To get started on T1 and T4, I have drafted an outline for the End-to-End Tax Documentation Workflow Map that will become A1, and a first pass at the roles list that will feed into A5 later.
Before we go deeper, can you share the main pain points you see today in how departments send data for tax, and which departments you think must be in scope from day one?

From what I see in the inbox and tracker emails, the biggest issues are late spreadsheets from operations and missing explanations for adjustments from finance.
For initial scope, I would definitely include accounting, finance, and operations. Sales sometimes sends rebate info that affects tax, but I am not sure if we want them in the first round or later.
For T1, I can help schedule short interviews with contacts in these areas so we can complete A1 properly.

From the tax side, I often receive incomplete documentation for deductible expenses and no clear link between invoices and the summary sheets.
I agree accounting, finance, and operations must be in scope. I would also add sales for items that impact VAT and rebates, otherwise we will still chase them manually.
Once T1 gives us a draft of A1, I can review the steps to make sure they match tax rules and our filing sequence.

From my side, I notice that we get different formats from each department, and sometimes people send PDFs instead of the spreadsheets we need.
For scope, I thought maybe we start only with accounting and finance to keep it simple, and then later add operations and sales once the process is stable.
I can help with T1 by listing the current documents we receive from each team, but I might need guidance on how detailed the process map in A1 should be.

If we leave operations out at the beginning, we might still have gaps for inventory and logistics related taxes. Maybe we can keep them in scope but limit it to the data they already send, without changing their tools yet.
For A1 under T1, I suggest we map at least: who sends what, in which format, and by when. We can refine the level of detail after the first round of interviews.

Good points. To balance risk and complexity, I would propose this initial scope for T1 and later T4:
- Accounting: full scope
- Finance: full scope
- Operations: limited to the data they already provide for tax
- Sales: limited to rebate and VAT relevant data
HR and legal can stay out of the first round, but we will note any touchpoints in A1.
If no one objects, we can treat this as the working scope for the first version of the workflow map.

Works for me. I can start scheduling interviews with accounting, finance, operations, and sales based on that scope so we can progress T1.
For T4, once we have A1, we can translate the steps into a RACI in A5. I am happy to draft the first version if someone else can validate the tax specific responsibilities.

I can review the RACI in A5 once you have a draft from T4, especially for who is accountable for tax calculations versus who just provides data.
On the workflow map A1, please include the step where we check documents against tax rules before filing, because that is often skipped in practice.

I am ok with including operations and sales in a limited way as you described.
For T1, I will start collecting examples of the current files from each department so we can see the differences when we build A1.
On T4, I am not sure who should be the final owner of A5. Maybe this should sit with accounting or with us as management assistants?

Given that A1 and A5 are cross departmental, it might be better if one of us in the assistant team maintains them, with tax and accounting validating changes.
I can support updates, but we should have a single named owner so there is no confusion when something changes in the workflow.

I agree that ownership should sit with the assistant team. Since I am already coordinating interviews for T1 and will draft the RACI for T4, I can take on the role of maintaining A1 and A5, as long as tax and accounting sign off on major changes.
We can define a simple change log so that updates are traceable.

Thanks, that works well.
To summarise where we are:
- Scope for the initial workflow map under T1 will cover accounting, finance, operations (limited to current tax data), and sales (rebates and VAT relevant data).
- HR and legal will be documented only as touchpoints if needed.
- A1 will reflect this scope, and T4 will translate it into A5.
- Ownership of A1 and A5 will sit with 60334, with tax and accounting reviewing significant changes.
Unless there are objections today, we will treat this as agreed scope and ownership.
No objections from my side. Once you have the first draft of A1 from T1, please send it my way and I will check that the tax review steps are correctly placed before filing.
All clear for me as well. I will focus on gathering the current documents and timelines from each department so that T1 has enough input for A1.
Fine by me. Once A5 is drafted under T4, I can help check that the roles are understandable for non finance staff before we share it more widely.

I will proceed with that scope and ownership.
Next steps from my side on T1 and T4: schedule interviews, draft A1, and then start the RACI in A5 for review.
Great, thanks everyone. We will track progress on T1 and T4 in the daily async check ins so that A1 and A5 are ready in time for the next phase.

threads.thread_goal: Design and sign off templates, tracker, and checklist for tax documentation.

messages.text:
I have prepared first drafts for the standard tax templates under T2: invoice summary, deductions list, and adjustments log. These will later feed into the Pre Filing Tax Documentation Checklist A4.
I also sketched the key columns for the central tracker A2 that will be built under T3: document type, period, department, status, owner, due date, and comments.
Could you please review the structure and let me know if anything important is missing before we finalise?

Thanks for sharing. On the templates from T2, I like that you separated deductions and adjustments.
For the tracker A2 under T3, I suggest we add: source system (if relevant), and a simple flag for items that are critical for the filing so we can prioritise follow up.
For A4, maybe we can group checklist items by department so people see exactly what they owe.

Looking at the invoice summary template from T2, could we include a field for tax code or rate category? That will help avoid misclassification later.
For the tracker A2, I would also add a field for last updated date and who updated it, so we can audit changes.
On A4, we should make sure there is a final confirmation step where the department contact signs off that their part is complete.

I had a quick look and I was wondering if we also need a free text field in the adjustments log for people to explain why they are making the adjustment.
For the tracker A2, I am not sure if we should track every single invoice or only summaries per period. Tracking every invoice might be a lot of work.

Good point on the volume. Maybe A2 should track document packages per period and department, not individual invoices. The invoice summary template from T2 can then list the details inside the package.
That way, the checklist A4 can refer to each package as a single line item.

Yes, I can add a reason field to the adjustments log template in T2.
On the tracker A2, I agree with 543897: we should track document packages per period and department, not each invoice. The invoice summary template will hold the line items.
I will update the drafts accordingly.

Agree on adding tax code or rate category to the invoice summary template under T2.
For A2, I propose the mandatory fields are: period, department, document package type, status, owner, due date, last updated date, and last updated by. Optional fields can be source system and priority flag.
If we align on this, I can start building the spreadsheet structure for T3.

The list of mandatory fields for A2 under T3 looks complete to me and still manageable for users.
On A4, I suggest we mirror some of these fields so that the checklist can be filtered by period and department when we do pre filing reviews.

I am ok with those mandatory fields for A2. It will help us see quickly who we need to chase.
For A4, could we add a simple yes or no column for each department to confirm that they checked their documents against the guidelines before sending them?

Yes, I can include a confirmation column in A4 as part of T2 deliverables, linked to the guidelines.
On the templates themselves, before we lock them, do you see any other tax relevant fields missing, such as withholding tax indicators or cross border flags?

We should add two more fields to the invoice summary template under T2: one for withholding tax yes or no, and one for cross border yes or no. That should cover most of the special cases we see.
If you incorporate that and the earlier comments, I would be comfortable treating the templates as our standard set for this rollout.

Once you add those two fields and the reason column for adjustments, I think the templates from T2 are ready to use.
For A4, I will help format the checklist so that it is easy to filter by department and period when we run the pre filing review.

Understood. I will update the templates from T2 with:
- Tax code or rate category
- Withholding tax yes or no
- Cross border yes or no
- Reason field for adjustments
Then I will run a quick check against tax rules to make sure we are not missing any mandatory data points.
After that, we can treat these as the standard templates for the rollout.
Perfect. I will start building the spreadsheet for A2 under T3 using the agreed mandatory fields and will link A4 to it so that we can test the flow in the next filing cycle.
Once A2 is ready, I can do a quick test run with one department to see if the fields are clear and if they can fill it without extra explanations. That will help us fine tune A4 as well.
Please share A2 once you have the first version. I want to check how we will record late items so that we can follow up properly.

To close this thread: we have aligned on the standard templates from T2 and on the mandatory fields and structure for the tracker A2 under T3, which will feed into the checklist A4.
Next step is to implement these in our existing spreadsheet tools and test them in the upcoming filing.

threads.thread_goal: Lock roles, responsibilities, and reminder/escalation rules.

messages.text:
I have drafted a RACI matrix for the new tax workflow under T4, which will become A5, and a first version of the reminder and escalation plan for missing data under T9.
The RACI covers the main steps from A1: data preparation in departments, consolidation, tax review, and filing. The reminder plan proposes weekly reminders starting three weeks before the deadline, with escalation to department managers one week before.
Please review and share any concerns before we lock this.

Thanks for putting this together. In A5, I noticed that operations is marked as responsible and accountable for some steps where they only provide data. I would keep them responsible but make accounting accountable for the final numbers.
On T9, weekly reminders might be too frequent at the start. Maybe we can do one reminder two weeks before, then weekly in the last two weeks, with escalation only in the final week.

From the tax side, I would like A5 to show tax as accountable for the tax review and filing steps, with accounting responsible for providing the underlying numbers.
For T9, we should also define who sends the reminders. I assume it will be the assistant team, but we need a clear name in the plan.

I saw that in A5 I am listed as responsible for updating the tracker and also for chasing all departments. I am a bit worried that this might be too much for one person.
Maybe we can share the chasing part across the assistant team, or at least have a backup in case I am out.

I can act as backup for reminders and escalations under T9. In A5, we can mark 27135 as responsible for day to day updates and me as alternate.
For the reminder schedule, I like the idea of increasing frequency closer to the deadline so people do not ignore early messages.

Good catch on operations. I will adjust A5 so that operations is responsible for providing data, while accounting remains accountable for the financial figures.
For T9, how about this schedule:
- Reminder 1: two weeks before deadline, to all department contacts
- Reminder 2: one week before, to contacts and copied to department managers for items still open
- Final reminder: two days before, with escalation to finance manager for any critical missing items
All reminders sent by the assistant team on behalf of accounting and tax.

This schedule for T9 looks balanced and should not overwhelm people.
On A5, please also make sure that tax is clearly accountable for the final filing step, with internal audit marked as consulted where needed.

I am fine with that reminder schedule under T9.
For A5, please list tax as accountable for: tax review, filing preparation, and submission. Accounting should be responsible for providing reconciled numbers and supporting documents.

Thanks for backing me up. With that change in A5 and T9, I feel more comfortable.
Just to confirm: I will send the first reminder two weeks before, and if I am away, 543897 will take over.

I have updated A5 accordingly under T4:
- Operations: responsible for data, accounting: accountable for figures
- Tax: accountable for tax review and filing
- Internal audit: consulted on key control steps
- 27135 responsible for tracker updates and first reminders, 543897 as backup
For T9, I will document the three step reminder and escalation plan you described.

With these adjustments, I am comfortable approving the RACI in A5 as the reference for the new workflow under T4.
We can still refine minor wording later, but the roles and accountabilities look correct.

Agreed. The RACI in A5 now reflects how we actually work and what we need for compliance.
On T9, I just want to confirm that the escalation to the finance manager two days before the deadline is acceptable from their side. We might need their formal confirmation outside this channel.

Good point. I will send the T9 reminder and escalation plan to the finance manager for confirmation.
For now, within this project, can we agree that the standard reminder frequency and escalation contacts are as documented, subject to their sign off?

Yes, from my side we can treat the reminder frequency and escalation contacts in T9 as agreed for the rollout, pending the finance manager confirmation.
This gives us a clear rule set to test in the pilot.
I am aligned as well. Once T9 is confirmed by the finance manager, I will help 27135 set up the actual reminder templates and mailing lists.
All clear. I will wait for the final T9 confirmation and then prepare the first reminder batch for the next filing period.

To wrap up: A5 under T4 is approved as our RACI reference, and we have an agreed reminder and escalation pattern under T9, pending formal confirmation from the finance manager.
We will now move on to implementing the reminder schedule in our email templates and linking it to the tracker.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and debrief the pilot run of the new workflow.

messages.text:
I propose that we use the upcoming monthly VAT filing for next month as the pilot for the new workflow under T7.
Scope would include accounting, finance, operations, and sales for that month only. We would use the new templates from T2, the tracker A2, and the checklist A4, and log any issues in the incident log A7.
If this works, we can then update the guidelines A3 and the incident procedure under T12 before the full rollout.

Using the next monthly VAT filing for T7 makes sense, as it touches most departments.
For the pilot scope, do we want to include all document types, or limit it to invoices and standard deductions first? That might reduce complexity for the first run.

I support using the next monthly VAT filing as the pilot under T7. It is frequent enough that we can still adjust before the quarterly deadline.
I would include invoices and standard deductions, but maybe exclude rare or complex adjustments for this first pilot, unless they are easy to map into the new templates from T2.

For the pilot, I would prefer to keep the number of departments small, but I see that VAT touches many areas.
If we go ahead, I will need clear instructions from A3 on how to fill A2 and A4 so that I can support the departments during the pilot.

We can prepare a short one page summary from A3 for pilot participants, focusing only on the steps they need to follow for A2 and A4.
That should make T7 smoother without waiting for the full guideline document.

I am fine limiting the pilot under T7 to invoices and standard deductions. We can log any complex adjustments that appear in A7 as incidents and handle them with the old process if needed.
So pilot scope would be: next monthly VAT filing, all four departments, but only invoices and standard deductions using the new templates from T2 and tracker A2.

That pilot scope for T7 sounds reasonable and low risk.
We should also define how we will capture feedback: I suggest we use A7 not only for discrepancies but also for process issues, and then summarise them into A8 after the pilot.

Agreed. I will update the pilot plan under T7 to reflect: next monthly VAT filing, four departments, invoices and standard deductions only, using A2, A4, and the templates from T2.
We can then schedule a short debrief meeting after filing to review A7 and start drafting A8.

Please let me know the exact dates for the pilot under T7 so I can plan my time for reminders and tracker updates in A2.
Also, how should we record small mistakes, like wrong department codes, in A7? Do they count as incidents?

For T7, I suggest we treat any issue that causes rework or delay as an incident in A7, including wrong department codes if they require correction.
We can group minor issues in one entry per department to keep A7 manageable.
That will also help when we draft the incident handling procedure under T12. We can use the grouped entries in A7 to identify the most common scenarios and write clear steps in A3 for each.

I will block the pilot period in our calendars and send a short summary from A3 to all participants, explaining how to use A2, A4, and the templates from T2 during T7.
After the filing, we will hold a 30 minute retrospective to review A7 and agree on changes for T8.

During the pilot under T7, I will monitor A2 and A4 closely and log any discrepancies or process issues in A7.
After the retrospective, I will consolidate the feedback and propose updates to the templates and guidelines under T8 and T12.

When you prepare the updates under T8, please highlight any changes that affect non finance users in A3 so we can adjust the training materials later.
We should also decide now how we will treat pilot feedback: do we want to apply all suggestions, or only those that reduce risk or effort?

I would suggest we classify pilot feedback from A7 into three groups for T8:
- Must have: compliance or control issues
- Should have: clear efficiency gains
- Nice to have: preferences or cosmetic changes
For this rollout, we commit to implementing the first two groups before go live. Nice to have items can go into a backlog for later.

That approach for T8 works for me. I will tag each A7 entry accordingly when I prepare the summary for A8 and the guideline updates in A3.
This way we can be transparent about which suggestions we implement now and which ones we park.

To summarise: we have selected the next monthly VAT filing as the pilot for T7, with scope limited to invoices and standard deductions across the four departments, using A2, A4, and the templates from T2.
We also agreed on how to classify and apply pilot feedback under T8, based on entries in A7 and the impact on A3 and A8.
This gives us a clear plan for the pilot and for post pilot adjustments.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate training sessions and final rollout communication.

messages.text:
I have prepared draft training slides A6 under T6, based on the guidelines A3 and the workflow map A1, and a tentative rollout timeline.
Proposal:
- Week 1 after pilot: two training sessions for accounting and finance
- Week 2: one session for operations and one for sales
- Go live for the new workflow at the start of the following month, with the post rollout report T10 and statutory books alignment T11 planned afterwards.
Please review and comment on the training content and dates.

The structure of A6 looks good. I like that you start with the big picture from A1 and then show concrete examples from A3.
On timing, I would keep at least one week between the last training and the go live date so people have time to digest and ask questions. Maybe we can move go live to mid month instead of the very start.

In A6, could we add a short section on common tax mistakes we saw during the pilot, using anonymised examples from A7 and the draft report A8? That will make the training more concrete.
For T10, I will need the final training dates to include them in the post rollout report.

For the sessions with operations and sales, I think we should keep the content very practical: how to fill A2 and the templates, and what happens if they miss a deadline.
Maybe we can shorten the theory part from A3 for those groups so we do not lose their attention.

Agree. For operations and sales, we can use a simplified version of A6 that focuses on their steps in A1 and the checklist A4.
I can help adapt the slides for those audiences under T6.

Good point on the buffer. How about this adjusted plan:
- Week 1 after pilot: accounting and finance sessions
- Week 2: operations and sales sessions
- Week 3: office hours for questions
- Go live at the start of Week 4
This still keeps us within the deadline for the next quarterly filing.

That timeline works for me and gives enough time for questions.
We should also define which groups are mandatory to attend. I would say: accounting and finance are mandatory, operations and sales at least one representative per team.

I agree with that. For tax, I will join the accounting and finance sessions to answer detailed questions and support the trainers.
In A6, please include a slide that clearly states which parts of A3 are mandatory rules and which are recommendations.

So we have:
- Mandatory attendees: all accounting and finance staff involved in tax, plus at least one representative from each operations and sales team
- Optional: others who work with tax related data
I will reflect this in the invites and in A6.
If there are no objections, we can treat these groups and the Week 4 go live as our plan.
No objections from me. I will help track attendance and share the slides A6 and guidelines A3 afterwards, as required by T6.
All good. I will support the operations and sales sessions and collect quick feedback so we can feed it into T10 and T11 if needed.

From tax, I am fine with the Week 4 go live date, as long as we do not move it closer to the quarterly deadline.
For T10, I will capture training attendance and timing as part of the context in the post rollout report.

Great. I will finalise A6 with the pilot learnings from A7 and A8, adjust the agenda per audience, and send out invites for the sessions under T6.
We can then confirm the official go live date as the start of Week 4 in our communication.

To close this: we have agreed on the training dates and mandatory attendee groups under T6, and we are confirming the go live date for the new workflow as the start of Week 4 after the pilot.
After go live, we will support T10 and T11 with data from the tracker and training feedback.
